**The main point**

The group walked through a data and platform architecture — covering a data foundation, clinical intelligence, member orchestration, and analytics tools — and discussed how those capabilities connect to actual member outreach. Mark and Catherine both said they could follow the technology logic but wanted clarity on what specific member interventions the system is meant to deliver; Catherine stated the company's intervention strategy — what to do with a member, when, how, and through which channel — is still a blank slate. Catherine raised a speed concern and said an external partner should at least be considered; Ratnakar said he agreed on pace and was open to acquisition, while Venkat noted the data-integration work cannot be outsourced. Kristy identified that pharmacy, Catherine's team, CareBridge, and others are already reaching the same members simultaneously with no shared visibility, and the platform meant to fix that does not yet exist for Caroline. A smaller meeting is set for the 20th to define required capabilities and accountability, but who owns member orchestration and clinical intelligence at the business level was explicitly left open.

**Presented, no challenge recorded**

- Monique presented that clinical intelligence is a single shared enterprise capability, with the goal of bringing clarity to capabilities and initiatives to drive value across strategic priorities.
- Venkat presented that the data foundation is a centralized store of administrative data, enriched continually by persisting predictions and clinical signals back into it; clinical data is acquired through HealthOS.
- Vikram confirmed Venkat's prediction work as accurate and noted that clinical intelligence predictions are longstanding, not new.
- Vikram presented that standardizing the model build, consume, and deploy pipeline is intended to enable innovation at scale.

**Open questions**

- Ashok raised: how to create small pods and execute at the member level.
- Ratnakar raised: what is the purpose and fit of each platform (member orchestration, HealthOS, TMB, TextQL, clinical intelligence) for member journeys and clinical outcomes.
- Ratnakar raised: which model performs better in driving the right outcomes, and how to know that without a neutral measure.
- Ratnakar raised: should the platform continue a multi-constituent model or shift to a single business and tech constituent model, and who arbitrates when conflicting next-best-action recommendations reach the same member.
- Catherine raised: which capabilities must be delivered and by whom — internal, external, or joint.

**Where people stand**

- Replicate existing model footprint for Caroline: Ratnakar supports, said "we're advocating we move forward with the Caroline Data Foundation."
- Hold a follow-up meeting, not on a Friday night: Ratnakar supports.
- Consortium or group manages enterprise orchestration: Stephen opposes if scope is defined broadly, said "it's so broad and it's so big."
- Parse clinical intelligence into discrete capabilities with smaller teams or single accountable owners: Stephen supports, said "I've been obviously suggesting."
- Retain company ownership of consumer relationship: Saurabh supports, said "let's not give that up."
- Engage external partner for clinical capability: Ratnakar is conditional — only if internal team cannot move fast enough — said "I agree with that."
- Proposed, no reaction recorded: build new models for Caroline; continue current multi-constituent model; shift to one business and one tech constituent; single individual owns orchestration; use AI to generate clinical journeys; acquire a strong external company; and 2 more.
- Catherine said "I'm not saying that we have to have a vendor, guys" and "I don't actually have a like a dog in that fight."
- Kristy said "we need to create the right journey so that we're all not going after the member at the same time" and that "things have to connect" across platforms via APIs.
- Ashok said "even if pick the right vendor… as long as we protect the member data and they do it within our ecosystem."

**What is blocking progress**

- The company has not defined when, how, or what to engage members on — Catherine called it a blank slate; which business leader aligns to Monique on clinical intelligence and which to member orchestration is unresolved (raised by Catherine).
- Who has authority to prioritize or suppress outreach when multiple teams reach the same member is unanswered; Ratnakar noted there are many models built by many different constituents (raised by Ratnakar and Kristy).
- Enterprise model rationalization deferred to the follow-up meeting (raised by Ratnakar).
- Single-person ID not yet enabled across all Caroline scope (raised by Ashok).
- Saurabh asked whether the company has the behavioral science discipline to define best engagement approaches (e.g., post-discharge); that question was not resolved.

**Next steps**

- Catherine will convene a small-group conversation on the 20th to define what the group is solving for, which capabilities are needed, and how they fit together.
- Ratnakar will outline the tech constituents on his side and identify Ashok as the clinical lead, and will map all constituents for the business and tech sides.
- Ratnakar will share the context from this discussion with tech-side stakeholders and business-side stakeholders.

**Awaiting a reply**

- Catherine asked who will be ultimately aligned to Monique on clinical intelligence and who should be aligned to member orchestration or member engagement; no reply recorded.
- Ratnakar asked whether enterprise orchestration should be owned by a single individual or a consortium; no reply recorded.

**Things people asserted that others may want to check**

- Ratnakar said the existing data footprint and model can be reused for Caroline as-is.
- Venkat said clinical signals and risk insights are already fed back into the data intelligence layer as current state.
- William said data centralization work over the next 6–12 months will further unlock enterprise capability.
- Ratnakar said everyone claims their own model is better and model superiority is hard to establish without a neutral measure.
